We are Stephen Kanti Mahanty and Ben Lertwachara at Harvey Mudd College. Our ENGR 155 project uses an STM32L432KC MCU and UPduino FPGA to control a suspended magnet and payload.

## Introduction

Our target is a **10 g total suspended mass**, including magnet, carrier, and object, moving between **10 and 20 mm surface gaps** below a 12 V electromagnet. Two Hall sensors sit above and below the electromagnet. The MCU combines their readings with measured current to estimate gap. The FPGA runs a position PI controller that sets PWM duty directly.

The hardware webpage will graph requested and estimated gap in real time, display current and faults, accept PI gain changes, and provide Stop. This report website describes that interface; the hardware control page is served separately.

## Project Status — November 10, 2026

The revised plan uses FPGA position PI, MCU ADC acquisition with DMA, and a **Heyiarbeit JF-XP2520-12V electromagnet** selected in the project discussion. The main application sources still implement the earlier MCU-position/FPGA-current design. Their recorded checks do not validate the revised controller.

A November 7 bench discussion reported receiving decimal **165**, or **0xA5**, from the FPGA on the MCU in a standalone SPI test. Levitation, calibrated resolution, stable motion, thermal operation, and shutdown timing remain unverified.
